scope: Player-facing read-only memory job progress and batch provenance; not automatic summary lifecycle or real-model quality

durableMemoryAndViewChecks: Dump/restore plus a separate process resumes the saved extraction without another model call
Recovered memory is retrievable by real pgvector and retains message/event provenance
Partial batch progress survives process restart and excludes interrupted replies
Replaying an already committed turn creates no duplicate job or memory
Enqueue and progress roll back with the story turn and recover on a subsequent commit
A crashed lease is reclaimed by only one of two concurrent workers
An expired worker cannot commit after replacement; checkpoint reuse avoids a second extraction
Zero vectors are failures; embedding recovery reuses extraction and writes no partial memory
Cross-story source references are rejected and retries stop at the configured cap
Explicit failed-job replay retains attempt history, checks reviewed state and cannot replay completed work
A valid empty extraction succeeds without embedding or a fabricated memory
Extraction has an abort deadline and a failed attempt is recorded
Over-budget sources stop visibly without truncation or a provider call
Editing source text during embedding prevents stale derived memory from committing
A message/event version mismatch is rejected before any extraction call
A database failure rolls back memory, vector and provenance together; retry uses the saved extraction
Deleting a story during extraction cascades work and rejects late completion without resurrection
Group participants count and derive independently within the same story
Group memory progress shows each frozen character and only their own five confirmed reply sources
A repeatedly crashed job stops at the retry cap instead of being claimed forever
Lowering the retry limit marks already exhausted queued work as failed instead of stranding it
Deleting completed work preserves other stories and every remaining provenance link stays in its confirmed story
Player view exposes real successful batch provenance and retained counts without returning memory text
Player memory reads reject another owner or tenant before loading jobs
Progress shows three confirmed replies before reaching the five-reply batch threshold
Extracted checkpoints, failure internals, digests and replay details never enter the player response
A source digest mismatch withholds references and never exposes the private digest
Queued, expired-running, retry, failed and completed-with-no-retained-memory states remain distinguishable
Foreign and missing pagination cursors fail identically
Bounded pagination preserves all batches sharing the same microsecond timestamp and global counts
Cross-story event references are withheld rather than becoming player source links
Interrupted or version-mismatched replies cannot be presented as confirmed memory provenance
Legacy stories explicitly report unsupported progress without inventing historical coverage
Deleted stories cannot return remembered progress or stale source IDs

browser.scope: Real API/WebSocket/browser/database; five controlled-provider turns. Failure/lease/success states and derived memory are explicitly seeded UI fixtures; real worker behavior verified separately.
checks: Empty automatic progress and saved personal notes remain distinct
Five real WebSocket turns create one durable batch; partial progress is visible after three
A controlled persisted failure is visible without exposing extraction or provider internals
Both source links open actual saved input and reply through the authenticated message API
Expired lease and retained-memory counts reflect database state; reads never trigger generation
Page reload preserves real progress; read failure is explicit, preserves last data, and recovers
390px memory panel exposes source controls without horizontal overflow and Escape returns focus

verification.visualReview: 1440px desktop failure state and 390px mobile source controls; mobile source click, dialog dismissal, Escape and focus return passed

limitations: No full automatic summarization lifecycle or old-history backfill.
Only batch provenance and retained counts are exposed, not unclassified derived text.
Memory job failure, expired lease and success states in browser are explicit database fixtures; worker behavior is validated separately in disposable databases.
Controlled providers do not prove real long-form coherence, knowledge isolation or phone hardware behavior.
EXP-05A/05B, EXP-07D and OPEN-01 through OPEN-07 remain open.
